title: Delimiting sections with triple backticks or XML markup

videos.script: A prompt reaches the model as one stream of text. Your instructions and the customer's words are the same kind of characters. {{title}} So you mark where the customer's words begin and end. The first mark most people reach for is three backticks. {{backticks}} Then a customer pastes a courier's note, and the note comes wrapped in backticks too. Now the prompt has four lines of them, and nothing says which pairs with which. Read as Markdown, the note falls outside the message. {{pasted}} The model read it the way a person would. On six pasted messages, backticks and tags gave the same answer every time. The measurement cannot choose between them. {{tags}} So the choice rests on what each mark guarantees. A tag has a name, customers rarely type one, and it can be escaped. A customer's error page that quotes the closing tag breaks the structure, and the escape mends it. {{escape}} What the escape does not do is stop the model obeying an order it finds inside the tags. By the end of this lesson you can mark what a prompt carries, choose a mark the content cannot close, and check it by rendering real cases. {{close}}
